instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Basically Finished
cards.instruction: Describe incomplete, late, or improvised work as a thoughtful version of completion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've finished your shelves along that diagonal pencil line you drew. A sloping display, just as planned.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That line crossed out the wrong position. I need somewhere to put books.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, away from the ordinary horizontal arrangement. The books can lean together; the display is complete.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They slide off. Fit one level shelf and I'll put the books there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One level shelf, of course. The finished reading section. We'll call the sloping ones the display section.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've finished the budget report. I blacked out every figure, like the copy you showed me. Ready for the board.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That was the public copy. The board needs to see what we're spending.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. This is the public edition, completed first. They can write their preferred figures beside the black bars.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They need your recommendation in ten minutes, not a colouring book.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll write 'Approve' at the bottom, then. A finished recommendation, with the confidential workings protected.

cards.title: I’ve Done This Before
cards.instruction: Perform calm familiarity with the task while learning how it works from every new clue.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll make your coffee. You gave this button a firm press; I'll start there too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's steam. I was cleaning it. The coffee button's behind the flap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, clean first. Now the flap. Where's your cup?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Here. It makes two cups unless you turn that dial.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dial to one. I always adjust it for the guest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You spread yours out so confidently, I've spread ours too. Pass the poles; we'll beat the rain.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're standing on the inner tent. Step off it; the poles clip to that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, inner first. I'll clip it up while you get the cover. Same system as yours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine's a pop-up. And your clips are underneath: you've laid it upside down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you take that end and we'll turn it. Much easier to check the clips before they're bearing any weight.

cards.title: Outdo the Effort
cards.instruction: Answer every favor, chore, or sacrifice with a bigger one that restores your lead.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You wrote 'cover' on the rota after giving me that lift. I've covered your whole weekend in correction fluid. Two days back for you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Cover means work for someone. I wrote it to give you Saturday off, not erase your shifts.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'll write my name in the space, then. You take Saturday and Sunday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm already off Sunday to drive you to the airport. Your plane leaves at six.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll move my flight. Leave your name off the rota all week; I'll cover your holiday before I take mine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You put a cross beside my name after bringing me dinner. I've put two beside yours; I'll cook for you twice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That cross means delivered, not owed. I've brought tomorrow's dinner too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Delivered, yes. I'll put four ready-made meals on your doorstep. Then you can mark them straight off.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm away all week. Just wash the dishes; I'll collect them when I'm back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave me your keys, then. I'll wash everything in your kitchen while you're away.

cards.title: Efficiency Win
cards.instruction: Celebrate each inconvenience as proof that a faster, cheaper, or smarter routine can now be invented.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've copied your double press on the lift button, then added two for the shopping bags. Saves us coming back for them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I pressed twice because it's stuck. We're walking up eight floors.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, the stairs today. Excellent, we can cancel the gym and do the full climb every evening.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: With all these shopping bags? I'll have to stop on every landing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Perfect, intervals. You choose the landings; I'll stop when you stop. A whole fitness class on the way home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've cleared the table, so I've put our clean dinner plates away. With the dishwasher broken, we can serve the curry in rolls.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only cleared the dirty plates. We've six rolls for twelve people.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, dirty plates first. Better still, halve the rolls: twelve edible bowls and the clean plates stay clean.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Those halves won't hold a dinner. We still need the plates underneath.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent, bread bowls on plates. Everyone can wipe up the curry with the bowl; we'll need half the washing water.

cards.title: No Trouble at All
cards.instruction: Remain gracious and accommodating while making your growing inconvenience impossible to miss.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've put your bag over your head against the rain; I'll carry your book bag that way too. No trouble, though the corners are firm.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine's waterproof. That's a paper bag of dictionaries. Let me take it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, waterproofing. I'll wrap it in my coat. Please, keep your hands free for the tickets.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We have to cross the bridge now. You can't hold that bundle up in this wind.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Quite right. I'll carry it under my coat instead. You lead the way; I don't mind a little rain down my collar.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've turned your empty plate over, so I've done mine too. Please give my pie to your brother; I'm quite comfortable with peas.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I turned it over because it's chipped. I haven't finished eating, and you haven't started.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, checking the crockery. Don't fetch another for me; peas sit quite nicely round the foot of this one.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll order you a pizza. It takes forty minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How kind. You all carry on eating. Leave me a place at the table until my dinner arrives, won't you?
